verdict.headline: Ready to cut · 0.000146 mm under the cut

limits: The cutting force is Kienzle's for a sharp tool, straight flutes (no helix), no run-out or wear, from the material's machinability group: a real tool and grade can differ by 20 % or more.
Only the part flexes: the tool, the holder and the spindle are rigid, so a stiff part cut by a long, slender tool chatters on the tool, which this does not see.

The cutter is put where the cut faces are most flexible along their normal, and only the force along that normal acts: the feed force along a wall is left out (turning: the tangential force, which bends a round part as much again, is counted in the stress).

Chatter is the zero-order (averaged) solution in one direction, the cut face's normal, linear in the chip: a light radial cut at high speed is interrupted enough to have extra lobes it misses, and at low speed the tool's flank rubbing the waves (process damping) makes the real cut more stable than this says.
The damping is the study's (2 % unless it says), not measured: a tap test on the clamped part gives the real damping and frequency, and the real lobes.
